brief: AI de-risking triggered a global positioning shock last week but hit markets unevenly. In the US, systematic and retail selling (not HF capitulation) drove Thursday's momentum unwind; buy-the-dip flows and Friday's AI/Semis rebound suggest investors are re-entering a cleaner trade, though UBS expects a final bout of Risk Control selling to mark a low on Monday. Asia saw more aggressive AI-led selling in Korea, Japan and Taiwan, with options clients monetizing hedges rather than rebuilding longs, while China and India drew counter-rotation buying as less AI-exposed markets. In Europe, the SXXP's flat +0.2% week masked a 2.5% intraweek reversal: the US midterm Democratic sweep reengaged rotation away from the AI supply chain (European Semis -10%, Defence -9.9%, RheinMetall -21% on a profit warning), while falling oil and rate volatility drove gains in Banks (+4.3%), Travel & Leisure (Airlines +11.7%) and Rate Cut Winners (+4.7%). Long-only de-risking was offset by hedge fund dip-buying and short covering; Prime data show HFs adding Banks and Autos longs while cutting Crowded Longs, Energy and Renewables exposure. Concerns over tighter US AI rules and slower data-centre deployment sharpened debate over AI-spending returns, pushing investors toward "ex-AI" opportunities; Healthcare kept drawing defensive demand, with the SXDP up 15% over the past month.
